title: Phased Pin & Exposure-First Onboarding Visuals (Canary, Variant Mix, Safety Fallback)
creator: Avery Chen
description: Design and deliver a compact, task-driven illustration and screenshot pack for the new quickstart that introduces users to staged releases and version pinning. The pack should make three core patterns obvious: phased canary exposure, A/B variant mixes with traffic sliders, and automatic fallback policies when a variant exceeds error/latency thresholds. Assets will be used in the Console quickstart flow, documentation, and the in-product guided tour.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A set of high-fidelity mockups for desktop and tablet that show: a) Create release -> Pin version b) Configure phased exposure (canary %) c) Define variant mix (A/B slider) d) Add fallback policy (thresholds + fallback target). 2) Illustration set (3) that visually explains the risk/reward tradeoffs (low exposure vs fast rollout). 3) Exported PNG/SVG assets and sample annotated screenshots for docs. 4) Accessibility audit (contrast ratios, text sizes, keyboard flows) completed and checklist attached. 5) Engineering sign-off on CTA placement and telemetry hook points.
design_notes: Aim for a minimal, stepwise visual language that maps directly to Console controls. Use an exposure-first metaphor (dial + horizon) rather than traffic maps used previously. Colors: use existing brand palette with one accent for 'pinned' state and another for 'fallback' state. Keep compositional grid at 16px baseline for Console parity. Create both a full-length walkthrough and a condensed 3-card hero set for docs header.
decisions:
- Use 'Exposure' label instead of 'Traffic' to reduce operator jargon.
- Replace static percentage chips with an interactive slider visual for A/B mixing.
- Fallback state uses a 'safety anchor' illustration (lifeboat) and red action token.
- Do not include server topology icons (avoid implying infra details).
